meta.policy: Zero Tier-3/secondary sources used for data values. Every source is Tier A (official government, statistical agency, Federal Reserve, regulator, or court/election body) or Tier B (official SEC EDGAR issuer filing) fetched live on 2026-11-08.

sources.publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), Western Information Office
sources.title: Los Angeles Area Economic Summary (Updated November 4, 2026)
sources.covers: Sep 2026 & Aug 2026 MSA/County/City unemployment, nonfarm payrolls by supersector, Q1 2026 QCEW average weekly wages, May 2025 OEWS hourly wage, Sep 2026 CPI-U & ECI, and consumer expenditure shares.

sources.publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS)
sources.title: Los Angeles Area Employment — September 2026 (Released November 4, 2026)
sources.covers: Sep 2026 preliminary LA-LB-Anaheim MSA nonfarm payrolls (6,282.1k, +30.2k / +0.5% YoY), LA-LB-Glendale & Anaheim MD breakdown, and Sep 2025–Sep 2026 industry changes.

sources.publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS)
sources.title: Consumer Price Index, Los Angeles Area — September 2026 (Released October 14, 2026)
sources.covers: Sep 2026 CPI-U (+3.7% YoY, +0.4% MoM), Core (+2.6%), Shelter (+3.7%), Food & Food-Away (+2.8%), Energy (+20.3%), Gasoline (+30.8%), plus Oct 2025 funding-lapse gap note.

sources.publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS)
sources.title: Employment Cost Index, Los Angeles–Long Beach CSA — September 2026 (Released October 30, 2026)
sources.covers: Sep 2026 12-month LA CSA private-industry ECI: +4.2% total compensation and +3.9% wages & salaries (vs +3.4% / +3.1% U.S. average).

sources.publisher: California Employment Development Department (EDD)
sources.title: Los Angeles County Labor Market Summary — September 2026 (la$pds.pdf)
sources.covers: Sep 2026 LA County SA unemployment (4.8% vs 5.0% rev. Aug 2026; 4.5% NSA), SA nonfarm jobs (4,539,800, +0.4% YoY), Limited-Service Eating Places (192,100, +1.5% YoY), and Motion Picture & Sound Recording (93,000, -7.3% YoY).

sources.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau
sources.title: QuickFacts: Los Angeles city, California & Los Angeles County, California (PST045225)
sources.covers: V2025 population (City 3,869,089; County 9,694,934), 2020–24 ACS median household income ($81,939 / $90,112), per-capita income ($47,685 / $45,792), poverty (16.5% / 13.3%), owner rate, rents, education, 2025 County permits (22,250), and 2022 Economic Census dining/retail sales.

sources.publisher: California Department of Finance (CA DOF), Demographic Research Unit
sources.title: E-1 City/County Population and Housing Estimates (Released May 1, 2026)
sources.covers: Jan 1, 2026 population: LA County 9,837,286 (-0.6% YoY; -64,000 loss across wildfires, domestic outflow, deportations), City of LA 3,806,201 (-0.9% YoY), CA 39,593,000 (-0.14%), and LA City +11,260 net housing units (+7,061 multifamily).

sources.publisher: California Department of Finance (CA DOF), Demographic Research Unit
sources.title: Revised July 1, 2025 County Population Estimates & Components of Change (Released February 4, 2026)
sources.covers: July 1, 2025 LA County population 9,853,435 (-44,822 / -0.45% vs Jul 2024 9,898,257), natural increase +20,997, net domestic migration -96,124, net foreign migration +30,305.

sources.publisher: California Department of Finance (CA DOF), Demographic Research Unit
sources.title: Public K-12 Graded Enrollment Projections (2026 Series, Released August 2026)
sources.covers: 10-year projection to 2035–36: LA County loses 240,800 public K-12 students (largest decline of any CA county); statewide public K-12 falls from 5,731,300 to 5,020,800 (-12.4%).

sources.publisher: California Department of Finance (CA DOF), Demographic Research Unit
sources.title: Population Projections Portal (Report P-2A, Vintage 2026, Released March 13, 2026)

sources.title: Documentary Transfer Taxes (County & City Schedules)
sources.covers: LA County documentary transfer tax $0.55 per $500 ($1.10/$1,000 = 0.11%) plus City of LA $4.50/$1,000 (0.45%) base and Measure ULA thresholds.

sources.title: Measure ULA — Real Property Transfer Tax FAQ (Thresholds Effective July 1, 2026)
sources.covers: Effective July 1, 2026: +4.0% City ULA surtax (4.45% City / 4.56% incl. County) > $5,400,000 to < $10,900,000; +5.5% surtax (5.95% City / 6.06% incl. County) >= $10,900,000, indexed annually each July 1.

sources.publisher: California Secretary of State & Legislative Analyst's Office (LAO)
sources.title: 2026 General Election Unofficial Returns (Nov 7, 2026), PR26-95 Withdrawal Notice & Prop 3 / Prop 43 Analyses
sources.covers: Initiative 25-0006A1 (ULA repeal) withdrawn Jun 25, 2026 (PR26-95); Prop 43 failing 56.8% No (43.2% Yes); Prop 3 passing 60.3% Yes, permanently extending CA high-income brackets past 2030.

sources.covers: Real-property-only tax deferral, strict 45-day identification / 180-day closing windows via Qualified Intermediary, boot & debt-relief rules (noting P.L. 119-21 OBBBA).

sources.covers: 12.30% top base bracket + 1.00% Behavioral Health Services Tax (> $1M) = 13.30% statutory cap-gains rate, annual Form 3840 clawback on out-of-state §1031 exchanges, and CA non-conformity to federal OBBBA.
